**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement's IP allocation meets the playbook's preferred position on every material term, with one point sitting at the fallback:

- **Our IP is never assigned away.** §7.1.1 (p0427–p0428) gives each Party sole ownership of its own inventions and its pre-existing/Controlled IP; §5.6.2 confirms no implied licences of AbbVie Patents or Know-How; and the only grant to Harpoon (§5.2) is a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free, non-sublicensable licence limited to performing the Initial Development Plan.
- **We own what we pay for.** §7.1.4(a) (p0432) requires each Party's personnel and subcontractors to assign results to that Party, channelling work product to us. §3.8.2(c) (p0327) makes all Regulatory Documentation, Regulatory Approvals and Product Labeling the sole property of AbbVie, with Harpoon obliged to execute confirmatory assignments — the data/dossier ownership sentence the rule looks for.
- **Vendor platform retention is acceptable.** Harpoon keeps its platform IP and licenses it to us exclusively under §5.1.3 for Exploitation of the Licensed Compounds/Products.

Two points noted in the rationale rather than flagged:

1. **Joint ownership exists** (§7.1.2), which is short of the preferred "no joint ownership." However, it is not walk-away territory: each Party may Exploit the Joint Intellectual Property Rights "without a duty of seeking consent from or accounting to the other Party," which is the unrestricted right to exploit the playbook requires. This sits at the fallback and is not redlined. The trailing "Notwithstanding the foregoing, with respect to (1) any [***], and (2) any [***]" carve-out is redacted in this copy — worth confirming against the unredacted text, but I did not treat unreadable text as a deviation.
2. **Reversion on termination** (§12.7.1) is a *licence* back to Harpoon, royalty-bearing and expressly excluding non-Licensed-Compound active ingredients and other AbbVie Patents/Know-How — not an assignment of our IP, and appropriately scoped for a terminated development/option deal.
